key_insight: UniClawBench introduces a universal way to evaluate proactive AI agents on realistic, everyday tasks instead of relying on narrow sandbox tests. It aims to separate different agent capabilities so benchmark scores reflect what models can truly do in the real world.
problem_solved: Current benchmarks often use simplified environments, single-turn evaluations, and mixed task categories that blur multiple skills together. This makes it hard to measure whether proactive agents can actually plan, act, and use real tools effectively in realistic settings.
method: Defines a universal benchmark designed for proactive agents operating in real-world tool-use scenarios.
Replaces overly simplified sandbox-style testing with tasks that better reflect everyday user environments and workflows.
Organizes evaluation so different model capabilities can be assessed more cleanly rather than being mixed within one task label.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this benchmark provides a more realistic and consistent way to compare agents. It can improve model selection, guide agent development, and reveal failure modes that traditional benchmarks miss.
visual_elements: A side-by-side comparison of traditional sandbox benchmarks vs. UniClawBench real-world tasks

paper_title: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
paper_authors: Zhekai Chen, Chengqi Duan, Kaiyue Sun, Bohao Li, Yuqing Wang
